clusters.state_of_play: The Iran war's economic fallout has deepened as Houthi rebels seized the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha, routing Yemeni government forces and gaining leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, while claiming Zuqar island and attacking the Hanish islands. The advance threatens Yemen's fragile truce, severs supply lines, and displaces thousands, opening a second theatre of war in the broader Iran conflict alongside earlier Houthi strikes on Saudi oil facilities across four cities that wounded more than 70 people. Saudi Arabia has threatened retaliation, and the escalation now imperils two key oil chokepoints -- Bab el-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz -- pushing Brent crude above $100 to as high as $105/barrel amid fears the war will not resolve quickly, also driving up borrowing costs, rattling global markets including a six-week low on Australia's ASX, keeping US gas prices at record highs, and complicating Trump's Iran deal push. Reports indicate Vice President Vance and Secretary Rubio have privately confronted Trump over his worst fears about the war's trajectory.
